review_notes.goal_0rk4jnw_1_p4_v1_s2_19u1y0d: The drill is present, not missing: live unit 42 at (-54, 54) covers four iron-ore entities and is idle without fuel. Its actual output is (-52.703125, 53.5). The placement receipt confirms a native candidate was used. However, this location is outside the committed checkpoint’s 8-tile radius around (-35.5, 63.5); the broader 24-tile guidance does not override that checkpoint. Keep the contract unchanged. Check native resource-bound candidates inside the required radius, then recover and relocate the existing idle drill if a legal candidate is available. Do not craft a duplicate or install the furnace at the current out-of-scope location. After relocation, inspect the drill’s fresh identity, resource coverage and output geometry. If no legal placement satisfies the committed radius, report that specific conflict rather than widening it.
review_notes.goal_0rk4jnw_1_p4_v1_s4_1lrmoah: Continue the unchanged active step. Fresh native observations show drill 43 at (-43,61) working and dropping directly into working furnace 44 at (-44,59); the earlier report that the drill was unfueled is superseded. Monitor the furnace's actual output and collect plates from that exact furnace, reducing the remaining collection deficit after each verified transfer until at least 58 plates are held. Use production/output monitoring rather than guessed wait durations; working production is not a blocker merely because the output is not ready yet. nodes.why_it_matters: After electronics and steam-power unlock the lab recipe, craft one lab and verify the automation-science-pack trigger technology is complete. Do not craft science packs before this unlock.

After steam-power is researched, establish a connected water, boiler, engine and electrical network that supplies a real load. Startup fuel may be supplied manually; automatic replenishment belongs to the fuel milestone.
Produce ten automation-science-packs only after their recipe unlock, supply a powered lab, and verify automation research is complete before crafting assembling-machine-1.

Extract fuel from natural resources and deliver it automatically to the chosen power and burner consumers. Verify any additional extraction or handling unlocks before building; exit when fuel replenishment needs no NPC transfers.
Natural iron ore feeds fueled smelting and plate extraction automatically. Verify output capacity covers the selected gear and science production rates.
Natural copper ore feeds fueled smelting and plate extraction automatically. Verify output capacity covers the selected science production rate.
An unlocked, powered assembler receives automatically produced iron plates and delivers gears without manual material inputs. Validate actual transport capacity.

Automatically produced copper plates and gears feed science assembly with automatic output removal and sustained power and fuel. Verify at least one automation-science-pack per minute over a full valid minute without manual replenishment.

steps.description: Prepare the copper bootstrap kit: hold 10 copper ore, 10 coal, and 1 stone furnace, reusing the held furnace.

execution_guidance.approach: Manually gather the missing 10 copper ore and 10 coal; preserve and reuse the held stone furnace.
execution_guidance.rationale: For only ten plates, manual bootstrap avoids placing, aligning and separately fueling the held drill. Direct feeding can pay back on later repeated demand; scaling has no proven cell yet.
constraints: Reuse the held furnace; do not craft a duplicate.
Coal is a startup reserve, not an exact burn estimate.
This manual supply does not establish automated capacity.

steps.description: Place the stone furnace at a legal nearby bootstrap site; inspect the placed furnace to obtain its exact live identity.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the held furnace at a legal nearby site, then observe its exact identity before any supply operation.
execution_guidance.rationale: A separate placement boundary provides the new live entity identity needed for exact supply and output verification. No miner-to-furnace geometry is needed for this finite bootstrap.
constraints: Presence proves installation only, not working smelting.
Do not invent a unit number or reuse an unobserved identity.
Keep placement local unless live terrain requires otherwise.

steps.description: Use the 10 copper ore and the coal reserve to smelt and collect 10 copper plates; verify electronics is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply the exact furnace with the gathered ore and sufficient reserve fuel; verify copper production, collect ten plates, and verify electronics.
execution_guidance.rationale: The native trigger requires production of ten copper plates through smelting, not a hand-crafting instruction. The step ends with ten held plates and electronics researched.
constraints: Observe the exact furnace before supplying or collecting.
Bind completion to copper-plate inventory >=10 and electronics researched.
Verify production and research; a transfer receipt alone is insufficient.

steps.description: Prepare the iron bootstrap kit: recover the furnace at (28, 96), retain the held burner mining drill, and hold 16 coal plus both machines.

execution_guidance.approach: Re-observe and recover the furnace at (28,96), reclaim its fuel, then gather only the deficit to 16 coal. Preserve the held burner drill and eight iron plates.
execution_guidance.rationale: Reuse avoids any machine crafting bill. Sixteen coal covers the modeled roughly 8 coal for mining and 4 for smelting fifty plates, with startup margin; reclaimed coal reduces gathering.
constraints: Refresh exact furnace identity before recovery.
Do not consume the eight held iron plates.
Count reclaimed fuel before gathering the deficit.

steps.description: Install the burner mining drill on the observed iron patch near (-35.5, 63.5); verify resource coverage and inspect its actual output position.

execution_guidance.approach: Move to the observed iron patch and use native resource-bound placement candidates for the held drill; inspect its placed identity and output geometry.
execution_guidance.rationale: One held burner drill yields 15 ore/min. The modeled fifty-plate direct-feed route takes about 203 seconds and frees the hands; manual mining alone occupies 100 seconds before supply and travel.
constraints: Require live iron resource coverage, not mere proximity.
Keep the installation within 24 tiles of (-35.5,63.5).
End at the fresh placed-drill geometry boundary.

steps.description: Install the recovered stone furnace over the drill's actual output point; inspect the new furnace identity and verify the direct ore connection.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the placed drill's actual item output as covers_position for native furnace candidates; place the recovered furnace and read fresh geometry/topology.
execution_guidance.rationale: A furnace must cover the real drill drop point. Its new identity and actual connection cannot be assumed before placement; this step separates that observation boundary from fueling.
constraints: Do not substitute the output point as a guessed furnace center.
Verify drill output targets this furnace.
Installation alone does not prove sustained operation.

steps.description: Fuel the iron cell from the 16-coal reserve, produce and collect 50 additional iron plates, and verify steam-power is researched; retain at least 58 iron plates total.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply approximately 10 coal to the drill and 6 to the furnace, verify working direct feed, then collect fifty new plates and verify the steam-power trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: The live trigger requires fifty iron plates produced by smelting. Retaining the eight starting plates means at least 58 held plates; this is construction bootstrap, not automatically fueled steady-state capacity.
constraints: Use exact freshly observed identities for supply and collection.
Bind completion to iron-plate inventory >=58 and steam-power researched.
Use output checkpoints for machine waiting, not guessed wait ticks.

steps.description: Prepare the copper bootstrap kit: hold one stone furnace, five copper ore and one coal; preserve the 58 iron plates and ten copper plates.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather five copper ore, five stone and one coal, less any freshly verified holdings; craft one stone furnace from the five stone.
execution_guidance.rationale: Five ore takes ten seconds of hand mining. A new furnace costs five stone and preserves the iron cell. Another drill adds setup for only five plates; a smelting row is unnecessary.
constraints: Preserve all 58 iron plates and ten copper plates during kit preparation.
Do not dismantle the existing iron cell.
Acquire only missing kit quantities.

steps.description: Place the new stone furnace nearby and inspect its fresh identity before supplying it.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the held furnace at an ordinary clear nearby location, then inspect its live identity and inventories.
execution_guidance.rationale: This finite hand-fed batch needs no precise transport layout. Placement ends at the new-identity boundary so subsequent supply targets the actual furnace.
constraints: Use the newly crafted furnace, not the operating iron furnace.
Read the new furnace identity before any exact transfer.
Presence alone does not prove smelting.

steps.description: Smelt the five copper ore in the new furnace and collect the plates, bringing held copper plates to at least 15.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply five copper ore and one coal to the new exact furnace; monitor its output and collect enough plates to hold at least 15 copper plates.
execution_guidance.rationale: Live rates give 16 seconds of furnace work and about 0.36 coal for five plates. One coal suffices; manual supply pays back sooner than installing a dedicated copper drill for this batch.
constraints: Use the freshly observed furnace identity.
Use output monitoring rather than guessed wait durations.
This bootstrap is not automated steady-state copper capacity.

steps.description: Craft one lab from ten gears, ten electronic circuits and four transport belts; verify automation-science-pack is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Refresh the lab bootstrap bill, craft only missing intermediates and one lab, then verify the exact automation-science-pack technology.
execution_guidance.rationale: The enabled lab recipe needs ten gears, ten circuits and four belts. Ten circuits require 30 cables from 15 copper plates. Crafting the lab satisfies the returned technology trigger.
constraints: Validate intermediate recipes and the combined remaining bill before crafting.
Verify both a held lab and automation-science-pack researched.
Do not craft science packs or locked assemblers in this slice.

steps.description: Smelt and collect one copper plate using the existing nearby furnace; retain the lab and at least 22 iron plates.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather one copper ore and startup coal, inspect the furnace near (18,109), then supply, monitor and collect one copper plate.
execution_guidance.rationale: Only one copper plate is needed for pole cables. Reusing the nearby furnace avoids another machine's crafting, travel and placement costs; a dedicated copper miner is unnecessary for this finite bootstrap.
constraints: Re-observe the furnace before exact transfers; its historical recipe is not current configuration.
Preserve the lab and at least 22 iron plates.
Monitor actual furnace output rather than guessing wait durations.

steps.description: Prepare the steam-kit materials: hold 52 iron plates, five stone, one wood, ten coal, one copper plate and the lab.

execution_guidance.approach: Collect available iron-cell output first; use its existing direct-fed drill and furnace for any remaining deficit. Gather five stone, one wood and ten retained coal.
execution_guidance.rationale: The combined bill is 42 iron plates for pump, boiler and engine, plus ten for spare pipes. Reusing the installed iron cell avoids new-cell setup; inspect stock and live rates before adding capacity.
constraints: Return to known iron-cell coordinates and obtain fresh identities before exact interactions.
Do not assume historical output or fuel remains available.
Finish with all six material quantities and the lab held simultaneously.

steps.description: Craft and verify the steam construction kit: one offshore pump, one boiler, one steam engine, two small electric poles and ten spare pipes; retain ten coal and the lab.

execution_guidance.approach: Refresh the combined bootstrap bill, craft missing intermediates and the five kit item types, then verify all kit contents and retained supplies.
execution_guidance.rationale: Ten gears and twelve consumed pipes, together with ten iron plates, make the three steam machines. One copper plate and one wood make two poles; ten extra pipes allow tentative connection routing.
constraints: Verify one pump, one boiler, one engine, two poles, ten pipes, ten coal and one lab.
Resolve actual missing dependencies before downstream crafts; do not duplicate satisfied items.
End at kit readiness; installation needs fresh water, placement and runtime geometry observations.

nodes.why_it_matters: Smelt iron from natural ore until the exact fifty-iron-plate production trigger completes steam-power; establish construction stock for subsequent milestones.
After electronics and steam-power unlock the lab recipe, craft one lab and verify the automation-science-pack trigger technology is complete. Do not craft science packs before this unlock.

After steam-power is researched, establish a connected water, boiler, engine and electrical network that supplies a real load. Startup fuel may be supplied manually; automatic replenishment belongs to the fuel milestone.
Produce ten automation-science-packs only after their recipe unlock, supply a powered lab, and verify automation research is complete before crafting assembling-machine-1.

Extract fuel from natural resources and deliver it automatically to the chosen power and burner consumers. Verify any additional extraction or handling unlocks before building; exit when fuel replenishment needs no NPC transfers.

steps.description: Prepare the copper bootstrap kit: hold 10 copper ore, 10 coal, and 1 stone furnace, reusing the held furnace.

execution_guidance.approach: Manually gather the missing 10 copper ore and 10 coal; preserve and reuse the held stone furnace.
execution_guidance.rationale: For only ten plates, manual bootstrap avoids placing, aligning and separately fueling the held drill. Direct feeding can pay back on later repeated demand; scaling has no proven cell yet.
constraints: Reuse the held furnace; do not craft a duplicate.
Coal is a startup reserve, not an exact burn estimate.
This manual supply does not establish automated capacity.

steps.description: Place the stone furnace at a legal nearby bootstrap site; inspect the placed furnace to obtain its exact live identity.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the held furnace at a legal nearby site, then observe its exact identity before any supply operation.
execution_guidance.rationale: A separate placement boundary provides the new live entity identity needed for exact supply and output verification. No miner-to-furnace geometry is needed for this finite bootstrap.
constraints: Presence proves installation only, not working smelting.
Do not invent a unit number or reuse an unobserved identity.
Keep placement local unless live terrain requires otherwise.

steps.description: Use the 10 copper ore and the coal reserve to smelt and collect 10 copper plates; verify electronics is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply the exact furnace with the gathered ore and sufficient reserve fuel; verify copper production, collect ten plates, and verify electronics.
execution_guidance.rationale: The native trigger requires production of ten copper plates through smelting, not a hand-crafting instruction. The step ends with ten held plates and electronics researched.
constraints: Observe the exact furnace before supplying or collecting.
Bind completion to copper-plate inventory >=10 and electronics researched.
Verify production and research; a transfer receipt alone is insufficient.

steps.description: Prepare the iron bootstrap kit: recover the furnace at (28, 96), retain the held burner mining drill, and hold 16 coal plus both machines.

execution_guidance.approach: Re-observe and recover the furnace at (28,96), reclaim its fuel, then gather only the deficit to 16 coal. Preserve the held burner drill and eight iron plates.
execution_guidance.rationale: Reuse avoids any machine crafting bill. Sixteen coal covers the modeled roughly 8 coal for mining and 4 for smelting fifty plates, with startup margin; reclaimed coal reduces gathering.
constraints: Refresh exact furnace identity before recovery.
Do not consume the eight held iron plates.
Count reclaimed fuel before gathering the deficit.

steps.description: Install the burner mining drill on the observed iron patch near (-35.5, 63.5); verify resource coverage and inspect its actual output position.

execution_guidance.approach: Move to the observed iron patch and use native resource-bound placement candidates for the held drill; inspect its placed identity and output geometry.
execution_guidance.rationale: One held burner drill yields 15 ore/min. The modeled fifty-plate direct-feed route takes about 203 seconds and frees the hands; manual mining alone occupies 100 seconds before supply and travel.
constraints: Require live iron resource coverage, not mere proximity.
Keep the installation within 24 tiles of (-35.5,63.5).
End at the fresh placed-drill geometry boundary.

steps.description: Install the recovered stone furnace over the drill's actual output point; inspect the new furnace identity and verify the direct ore connection.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the placed drill's actual item output as covers_position for native furnace candidates; place the recovered furnace and read fresh geometry/topology.
execution_guidance.rationale: A furnace must cover the real drill drop point. Its new identity and actual connection cannot be assumed before placement; this step separates that observation boundary from fueling.
constraints: Do not substitute the output point as a guessed furnace center.
Verify drill output targets this furnace.
Installation alone does not prove sustained operation.

steps.description: Fuel the iron cell from the 16-coal reserve, produce and collect 50 additional iron plates, and verify steam-power is researched; retain at least 58 iron plates total.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply approximately 10 coal to the drill and 6 to the furnace, verify working direct feed, then collect fifty new plates and verify the steam-power trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: The live trigger requires fifty iron plates produced by smelting. Retaining the eight starting plates means at least 58 held plates; this is construction bootstrap, not automatically fueled steady-state capacity.
constraints: Use exact freshly observed identities for supply and collection.
Bind completion to iron-plate inventory >=58 and steam-power researched.
Use output checkpoints for machine waiting, not guessed wait ticks.
